key_insight: A symmetry-preserving ADAPT-SSVQE quantum algorithm can simultaneously recover multiple nuclear shell-model eigenstates in one run, helping bypass the classical Hilbert-space scaling barrier.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical quantum workflow for many-body nuclear structure calculations, with a circuit design that targets a physically constrained subspace and reduces the need for separate excited-state post-processing.
method: Map the nuclear Hamiltonian from fermionic bits to qubits using the Jordan-Wigner transformation.
Use SSVQE with an ADAPT ansatz built from symmetry-preserving single and double excitation operators.
Optimize a weighted energy sum to converge multiple orthogonal eigenstates within a chosen M_J subspace.
evidence_signal: In simulation, the method extracted five states for two identical nucleons and ten states for three identical nucleons in a j=9/2 orbital using a 10-qubit active space, matching exact diagonalization with spectroscopic accuracy.
watch_item: The results are currently simulation-based and rely on a targeted symmetry subspace, so performance under real hardware noise and for larger shell-model spaces remains to be demonstrated.
paper_title: Full-Spectrum Quantum Simulation for the Nuclear Shell Model
